title.raw: How to build dead link checker of some webpage
title.rendered: How to build dead link checker of some webpage

content.raw:
Step #1:

We will need to fetch all existed links on that webpage

We can achieve that using JavaScript on console of the webpage 

in es6

let $uniqueLinks = [...document.links].map(l => l.href).filter((value, index, array) => array.indexOf(value) === index);

So now we have all unique urls on the current opened page

We need to save this list of links into some file

In the console we paste this code in console which will add console.save method that will create a FileBlob from the input, and then automatically downloads it.

(function(console){

    console.save = function(data, filename){

        if(!data) {

            console.error('Console.save: No data')

            return;

        }

        if(!filename) filename = 'webpage-urls.json'

        if(typeof data === "object"){

            data = JSON.stringify(data, undefined, 4)

        }

        var blob = new Blob([data], {type: 'text/json'}),

            e    = document.createEvent('MouseEvents'),

            a    = document.createElement('a')

        a.download = filename

        a.href = window.URL.createObjectURL(blob)

        a.dataset.downloadurl =  ['text/json', a.download, a.href].join(':')

        e.initMouseEvent('click', true, false, window, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, false, false, false, false, 0, null)

        a.dispatchEvent(e)

    }

})(console)

Now just write console.save($uniqueLinks) in console to download the list

We have now all webpage links in json file “webpage-urls.json”

Step #2:

We need to ping all of these links and check if response 404, we can write small bash that will accept file of links and ping each line

#!/bin/bash

# Function to check URLs using curl

check_url() {

    local url=$1

    local response=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$url")

    # Check if the response code is 404

    if [ "$response" -eq 404 ]; then

        echo "Not Found: $url"

    fi

}

# Read each URL from the file and check using check_url function

while IFS= read -r url; do

    check_url "$url"

done < webpage-urls.json

title.raw: How to send email with input attachments in Next.Js using Nodemailer and Formidable
title.rendered: How to send email with input attachments in Next.Js using Nodemailer and Formidable

content.raw:
1. First, make sure you have the necessary dependencies installed:
npm install express formidable nodemailer

2. Create an API route that handles file uploads and sends an email:

Create a file called send-email.js in the pages/api directory:

// pages/api/send-email.js

import nodemailer from 'nodemailer';
import formidable from 'formidable';
import fs from 'fs';

export const config = {
    api: {
        bodyParser: false,
    },
};

const transporter = nodemailer.createTransport({
    host: process.env.SMTP_HOST,
    port: parseInt(process.env.SMTP_PORT),
    auth: {
        user: process.env.SMTP_USER,
        pass: process.env.SMTP_PASSWORD,
    },
    secure: false, // @TODO khaled: change this
});

export default async (req, res) => {
    if (req.method !== "POST") {
        res.status(405).send("Method not allowed");
        return;
    }
    const form = new formidable.IncomingForm();

    form.parse(req, async (err, fields, files) => {
        if (err) {
            return res.status(400).json({error: 'Error parsing form data'});
        }

        const {
            name,
            email,
            message,
        } = fields;


        // @TODO khaled: you can add some validations here e.g.
        if (name.length < 1) {
            return res.status(403).json({message: 'Name can not be empty'});
        }


        try {

            const mailData = {
                from: process.env.SMTP_FROM,
                to: [process.env.ADMIN_EMAIL],
                subject: `Message From ${name}`,
                text: "Name: " + name + " | Message: " + message + " | Email: " + email,
                html: `<p>Name: ${name}</p><p>Message: ${message}</p><p>Email: ${email}</p>`,
                attachments: Object.values(files).map((file: File) => {

                    // @TODO khaled: you can add some validations here e.g. validate allowed file types
                        return {
                            filename: file?.name,
                            content: fs.createReadStream(file.path)
                        }
                    }
                    return null;
                })
            };

            await transporter.sendMail(mailData);

            return res.status(200).json({message: 'Email sent successfully'});
        } catch (error) {
            console.error(error);
            return res.status(500).json({error: 'Email could not be sent'});
        }
    });
}
